assumptions: Cover crop growth follows a temperature curve to full cover at about 700 °C-days (base 0 °C); real stands vary with seeding date and rate.
Residue cover after harvest comes from ISU PM 1901a; how fast it breaks down is an assumption by residue type.

The yield index is % of a water-unlimited potential at this site (FAO-33 Ky method). For US counties with USDA NASS yield records, the county yield range in bu/ac comes from M2 and sets the yield scale for profit; it describes the county average, not your field.
Erosion uses RUSLE with a 50 m slope length and no conservation practice factor (P = 1).
Weather is NASA POWER at ≈50 km: it describes the region around the field, not the field itself.
reminder: FarmSmart shows patterns and trade-offs. It does not replace your judgment or local agronomy advice.
